Transversal Hadamard turns the patch

Apply H to every data qubit of the canonical d=3d=3d=3 patch.

  1. Write the transformed check table. Is its stabilizer group unchanged?
  2. Relabel by q(r,c)↦q(c,2−r)q(r,c)\mapsto q(c,2-r)q(r,c)↦q(c,2−r), with zero-based row and column coordinates. Give the label permutation and track both logicals.
  3. Which couplings stay fixed, and which check-extraction operations and boundary roles change? Why can the hardware still need patch rotation?
  4. What happens to a rectangular patch with (dX,dZ)=(3,5)(d_X,d_Z)=(3,5)(dX​,dZ​)=(3,5)? Explore rectangular memories further.
  5. How did Satzinger's preparation compensate for this rotation, and why does Steane's transversal H need no such relabeling?

Optional: suppose conjugation by the full local unitary circuit spreads an operator by at most rrr lattice spacings. Use a light cone to show why r<d−1r<d-1r<d−1 prevents logical H on the fixed patch.

Hint

H exchanges X and Z at unchanged sites. Compare supports after the quarter turn, then compare the transformed logicals modulo check products.

Check against the rubric
  • Swaps all check letters and shows the original group is not preserved by H alone.
  • Gives the quarter-turn permutation and logical X/Z exchange.
  • Separates coupling supports, extraction schedule and boundary orientation.
  • Exchanges the rectangular distances and identifies Steane's equal CSS row spaces.
Show model solution

The new X supports are {2,3,5,6},{4,5,7,8},{1,4},{6,9}\{2,3,5,6\},\{4,5,7,8\},\{1,4\},\{6,9\}{2,3,5,6},{4,5,7,8},{1,4},{6,9}; new Z supports are {1,2,4,5},{5,6,8,9},{2,3},{7,8}\{1,2,4,5\},\{5,6,8,9\},\{2,3\},\{7,8\}{1,2,4,5},{5,6,8,9},{2,3},{7,8}. This is a different group: for example, X1X4X_1X_4X1​X4​ anticommutes with the original Z-b check and was not an original stabilizer.

The clockwise turn relabels the sites as

1→3,2→6,3→9,4→2,5→5,6→8,7→1,8→4,9→7.1\to3,\quad2\to6,\quad3\to9,\quad4\to2,\quad5\to5,\quad 6\to8,\quad7\to1,\quad8\to4,\quad9\to7.1→3,2→6,3→9,4→2,5→5,6→8,7→1,8→4,9→7.

It sends new X supports to original X-b, X-a, X-c, X-d respectively, and new Z supports to original Z-a, Z-b, Z-d, Z-c. On logicals,

Xˉ→H⊗9Z1Z4Z7→turnZ3Z2Z1=Zˉ,Zˉ→H⊗9X1X2X3→turnX3X6X9∼Xˉ.\bar X\xrightarrow{H^{\otimes9}}Z_1Z_4Z_7\xrightarrow{\rm turn}Z_3Z_2Z_1=\bar Z, \qquad \bar Z\xrightarrow{H^{\otimes9}}X_1X_2X_3\xrightarrow{\rm turn}X_3X_6X_9\sim\bar X.XˉH⊗9​Z1​Z4​Z7​turn​Z3​Z2​Z1​=Zˉ,ZˉH⊗9​X1​X2​X3​turn​X3​X6​X9​∼Xˉ.

The right-column operator obeys X3X6X9=Xˉ⋅X-a⋅X-b⋅X-c⋅X-dX_3X_6X_9=\bar X\cdot\text{X-a}\cdot\text{X-b}\cdot\text{X-c}\cdot\text{X-d}X3​X6​X9​=Xˉ⋅X-a⋅X-b⋅X-c⋅X-d. Thus H followed by the permutation implements logical H. Before relabeling, all eight check supports and their couplers stay fixed. Each measure qubit extracts the opposite Pauli, changing its preparation/readout basis and gate schedule. Boundary roles exchange too. Physical rotation or deformation can restore their orientation relative to neighboring patches.

The rectangular memory becomes (5,3)(5,3)(5,3), so H alone does not preserve an asymmetric memory. Satzinger rotated the ∣0L⟩|0_L\rangle∣0L​⟩ preparation circuit by 90 degrees before adding transversal H Realizing topologically ordered states on a quantum processor, PDF p. 9, supplement Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1126/science.abi8378. Steane's X and Z check row spaces are equal, so H already preserves its group.

For the optional proof, conjugating a top-row Zˉ\bar ZZˉ spreads its support by at most the full circuit's propagation radius rrr. If r<d−1r<d-1r<d−1, the result is disjoint from a bottom-row Zˉ\bar ZZˉ and commutes with it. A logical X must anticommute with that equivalent Z representative, so the circuit cannot implement logical H Quantum error correction for quantum memories, PDF p. 30 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1103/RevModPhys.87.307.

Decode the 17-qubit patch, and count what fools it

Use the canonical d=3d=3d=3 check table. Assume independent X errors with probability ppp per data qubit, perfect checks, and a minimum-weight X lookup recovery for each Z-check syndrome.

  1. List every single-X syndrome in a,b,c,d order. Which collisions are harmless?
  2. Which single errors flag exactly one check? Explain the contrast with a torus.
  3. Decode X1X4X_1X_4X1​X4​. Count failing weight-two supports and determine whether logical-class ties matter.
  4. List all weight-three X logicals. Translate Tomita–Svore's zero-based X2X4X6X_2X_4X_6X2​X4​X6​ and express it as Xˉ\bar XXˉ times checks. Why do straight columns underestimate the leading failures by a factor of two?
  5. At d=5d=5d=5, exhaustive enumeration gives 52 minimum X logicals and 292 failing weight-three supports among 2,300, with no logical-class ties. Estimate PL(3)/PL(5)P_L(3)/P_L(5)PL​(3)/PL​(5) at p=10−2p=10^{-2}p=10−2 and 10−310^{-3}10−3. What carries over to circuit-level data, and what changes?

Hint

Syndromes add modulo two. A weight-two error fails when its shortest recovery completes a logical. To find minimal logicals, choose exactly one site from each of the three disjoint Z-logical rows and test the checks.

  • Explains single flags by boundary absorption.

  • Lists eight logical supports and translates the source's labels correctly.
  • Computes both leading-order ratios and distinguishes a coefficient from a threshold.

Each pair drawn from one of these supports leaves a single site to complete a logical. After removing duplicate pairs, the 18 failures are:

{14,17,18,25,26,27,28,29,35,36,37,38,39,47,48,57,58,69}.\{14,17,18,25,26,27,28,29,35,36,37,38,39,47,48,57,58,69\}.{14,17,18,25,26,27,28,29,35,36,37,38,39,47,48,57,58,69}.

A weight-two error times a weight-two recovery has even weight. Every X check also has even weight, while Xˉ\bar XXˉ has odd weight, so every nontrivial X logical has odd weight. A weight-two recovery therefore cannot differ logically from a weight-two error. Every weight-two failure uses a weight-one recovery and appears in the list. Equal-weight recoveries likewise cannot differ by a logical X, so tie-breaking cannot change these outcomes. Straight columns give only 3(32)=93\binom32=93(23​)=9 pairs; staircase logicals supply the rest.

A rectangular rotated memory

Take odd dXd_XdX​ data rows and odd dZd_ZdZ​ columns, with dX≠dZd_X\ne d_ZdX​=dZ​. Keep the checkerboard and half-check rules: X above/below, Z left/right. Derive the data and check counts, kkk, and both logical distances. Compare a three-row, five-column patch with its transpose. Which noise bias could favor each orientation? Which circuit and decoder assumptions would turn that design argument into a performance prediction?

Hint

An X column traverses rows. A Z row traverses columns. Use disjoint transverse representatives for the lower bounds, not only visible paths.

  • Proves dXd_XdX​ is the X-logical distance and dZd_ZdZ​ the Z-logical distance.

Count (dX−1)(dZ−1)(d_X-1)(d_Z-1)(dX​−1)(dZ​−1) full faces, dZ−1d_Z-1dZ​−1 horizontal X half-checks, and dX−1d_X-1dX​−1 vertical Z half-checks:

Nchecks=(dZ−1)(dX−1)+(dX−1)+(dZ−1)=dXdZ−1.N_{\rm checks}=(d_Z-1)(d_X-1)+(d_X-1)+(d_Z-1)=d_Xd_Z-1.Nchecks​=(dZ​−1)(dX​−1)+(dX​−1)+(dZ​−1)=dX​dZ​−1.

Every same-type check component reaches the exterior, so the coefficient-propagation proof makes these checks independent. With dXdZd_Xd_ZdX​dZ​ data qubits, k=dXdZ−(dXdZ−1)=1k=d_Xd_Z-(d_Xd_Z-1)=1k=dX​dZ​−(dX​dZ​−1)=1. One measure qubit per check gives total 2dXdZ−12d_Xd_Z-12dX​dZ​−1.

An X column has weight dXd_XdX​. Any X logical must cross each of the dXd_XdX​ disjoint Z rows, so none is lighter. Exchanging X and Z proves Z distance dZd_ZdZ​. A mixed Pauli cannot have less support than its nontrivial component, giving general distance min⁡(dX,dZ)\min(d_X,d_Z)min(dX​,dZ​).

Three rows and five columns use 15 data qubits and 14 checks, totaling 29, with distances (dX,dZ)=(3,5)(d_X,d_Z)=(3,5)(dX​,dZ​)=(3,5). Euler counts the logical qubits; then add a handle

For a connected cellulation of a closed orientable surface:

  1. Prove k=E−(V−1)−(F−1)=2−χk=E-(V-1)-(F-1)=2-\chik=E−(V−1)−(F−1)=2−χ, and identify β0\beta_0β0​ and β2\beta_2β2​.
  2. A honeycomb torus has NNN hexagonal faces. Find V,E,FV,E,FV,E,F, check weights and kkk.
  3. Remove one face from each of two L=3L=3L=3 tori and identify their four-edge boundaries. Find V,E,FV,E,FV,E,F, both check ranks, kkk and the exceptional star weights.
  4. The seam is a separating four-edge loop. Is its Z operator logical? Can the loop be contracted to a point?

Hint

Connected primal and dual incidence matrices each have one relation. When gluing, identify four vertex pairs and four edge pairs; delete two faces. Multiply the remaining faces of one punctured torus to test the seam.

Check against the rubric
  • Proves both rank formulas and obtains k=2gk=2gk=2g.
  • Counts honeycomb vertices and edges from incidences.
  • Computes the glued ranks and the four weight-six seam stars.
  • Distinguishes a homologically trivial separating loop from a contractible loop.
  • Connects negative Euler characteristic with average degree above four.
Show model solution

An identity star product requires equal selection bits across every edge. Connectivity leaves only the empty and full products, giving rank V−1V-1V−1. Dual connectivity gives face rank F−1F-1F−1. The dependencies correspond to β0=β2=1\beta_0=\beta_2=1β0​=β2​=1: one connected component and one closed surface. Thus k=E−V−F+2=2−χ=2gk=E-V-F+2=2-\chi=2gk=E−V−F+2=2−χ=2g for this code on a connected closed orientable surface.

For the honeycomb torus, edge-face incidences give 6N=2E6N=2E6N=2E, and degree-three vertices give 3V=2E3V=2E3V=2E. Hence (V,E,F)=(2N,3N,N)(V,E,F)=(2N,3N,N)(V,E,F)=(2N,3N,N), with star weight three, face weight six, and k=2k=2k=2.

Two L=3L=3L=3 tori start with (18,36,18)(18,36,18)(18,36,18). Delete one face from each and identify four pairs of vertices and edges:

(V,E,F)=(14,32,16),χ=−2,(rX,rZ)=(13,15),k=4.(V,E,F)=(14,32,16),\quad\chi=-2,\quad(r_X,r_Z)=(13,15),\quad k=4.(V,E,F)=(14,32,16),χ=−2,(rX​,rZ​)=(13,15),k=4.

Each of the four seam vertices has two perimeter edges and four outward edges, giving weight six. The other ten stars retain weight four. The eight remaining faces of either punctured torus cancel internally, leaving the seam as their boundary. Its Z loop is therefore a stabilizer, although the loop separates the handles and cannot contract to a point.

Square faces give 4F=2E4F=2E4F=2E, hence χ=V−E/2\chi=V-E/2χ=V−E/2. Negative χ\chiχ requires 2E/V>42E/V>42E/V>4, so some vertex has degree above four. Topology fixes kkk; shortest nontrivial paths determine distance. Thresholds also depend on noise and decoding. Tangent: a hole is an internal boundary

Optional. Stop measuring one Z plaquette in an all-smooth disk. The check rank drops by one, so kkk rises from zero to one. The missing check becomes Zˉ′\bar Z'Zˉ′; a dual X string to the exterior X-boundary is its conjugate Xˉ′\bar X'Xˉ′. The m endpoint at the missing detector is invisible. Name the hole by its missing check, since sources reverse “primal” and “dual” hole names.

A missing square face gives distance min⁡(4,Dp)\min(4,D_p)min(4,Dp​), where DpD_pDp​ is the shortest dual path to the outside. On a 5×55\times55×5 vertex disk, face (1,1)(1,1)(1,1) gives (dX,dZ)=(2,4)(d_X,d_Z)=(2,4)(dX​,dZ​)=(2,4) and a corner gives (1,4)(1,4)(1,4). Face (2,2)(2,2)(2,2) on a 6×66\times66×6 disk gives (3,4)(3,4)(3,4). Coordinates start at zero.

A genuine m×mm\times mm×m square hole has perimeter 4m4m4m; hhh such holes encode hhh qubits. Making one requires removing interior degrees of freedom and changing checks. Leaving m2m^2m2 independent checks unmeasured instead adds many logical degrees of freedom. Turn off one check

Use the canonical rotated check table and treat an unmeasured check as absent, without changing the data qubits or other checks.

  1. Remove Z-a at d=3d=3d=3. Find kkk, every single-qubit logical Pauli, and the new distance. Interpret its invisible endpoint.
  2. Remove one bulk Z check at d=5d=5d=5. Find the ranks and identify the added logical pair.
  3. Treat the added qubit as gauge: its state will not be protected. Choose its X as a shortest string from the missing face to the nearer X-boundary. Let wtop,wbottomw_{\rm top},w_{\rm bottom}wtop​,wbottom​ be the shortest X-string weights to those boundaries. The retained qubit's dressed distance allows arbitrary action on the gauge qubit. Show that its dressed X distance is min⁡(5,max⁡(wtop,wbottom))\min(5,\max(w_{\rm top},w_{\rm bottom}))min(5,max(wtop​,wbottom​)). Evaluate a middle and an outer face row. Does the Z distance change?
  4. What is the loop weight around a genuine m×mm\times mm×m square hole, and why use large holes?
  5. Why do 49 data and 97 data-plus-measure qubits alone not certify distance on a defective chip?

Hint

Deleting an independent check adds a logical degree of freedom. The missing check is one new logical; a string that anticommutes with it but commutes with all measured checks is its partner. Distinguish the three nonzero X classes before selecting which is gauge.

Check against the rubric
  • Finds ranks four and three at d=3d=3d=3, with only X2,X3X_2,X_3X2​,X3​ as single-site logicals.
  • Identifies the missing Z check and a boundary-to-hole X string as a pair.
  • States the gauge choice and compares all three nonzero X classes.
  • Gives dressed distances (3,5)(3,5)(3,5) or (4,5)(4,5)(4,5) and explains the unchanged Z quotient.
  • Separates a large physical hole from multiple missing independent checks, and qubit count from distance.
Show model solution

At d=3d=3d=3, ranks (rX,rZ)=(4,3)(r_X,r_Z)=(4,3)(rX​,rZ​)=(4,3) leave k=9−4−3=2k=9-4-3=2k=9−4−3=2. Only X2,X3X_2,X_3X2​,X3​ among single-site Paulis commute with all measured checks without being stabilizers. They differ by X-c, so they represent one weight-one logical class. The full-code distance is one. Their m endpoint is invisible at the missing Z detector, one step from the top X-boundary. Choosing X2X_2X2​ and missing Z-a as gauge X and Z instead leaves a protected qubit with dressed distances (dX,dZ)=(2,3)(d_X,d_Z)=(2,3)(dX​,dZ​)=(2,3).

At d=5d=5d=5, ranks 12 and 11 on 25 data sites give k=2k=2k=2. The missing Z check commutes with every remaining check. A dual X string from it to an X-boundary crosses it once, forming the added logical pair. For the middle-row face Z-c on {6,7,11,12}\{6,7,11,12\}{6,7,11,12}, the full code has X/Z distances (2,4)(2,4)(2,4), attained by the shorter boundary string and the missing check.

To protect only one qubit, compare the three nonzero X classes modulo X checks: old Xˉ\bar XXˉ, top-to-hole ggg, and bottom-to-hole gXˉg\bar XgXˉ. Their minimum weights are 5,wtop,wbottom5,w_{\rm top},w_{\rm bottom}5,wtop​,wbottom​. Choose the shorter boundary string as gauge X, paired with the missing Z check. The other two classes represent the retained logical, up to gauge action:

dXdressed=min⁡(5,max⁡(wtop,wbottom)).d_X^{\rm dressed}=\min(5,\max(w_{\rm top},w_{\rm bottom})).dXdressed​=min(5,max(wtop​,wbottom​)).

Middle face rows have boundary weights {2,3}\{2,3\}{2,3}, giving dressed X distance three; outer rows have {1,4}\{1,4\}{1,4}, giving four. Restoring the missing Z check to the gauge span restores the original Z-logical quotient, so dZ=5d_Z=5dZ​=5. These distances belong to this chosen subsystem; a different gauge choice can select different protected information.

A genuine m×mm\times mm×m hole has perimeter logical weight 4m4m4m and a conjugate path to an absorbing boundary. Both lengths limit distance. Reconstruct the entropy subtraction

Read Satzinger et al., PDF pp. 2–3, Eq. (3) and Fig. 2.

  1. Derive ρA=2−∣A∣∑g∈SAg\rho_A=2^{-|A|}\sum_{g\in S_A}gρA​=2−∣A∣∑g∈SA​​g and the stabilizer entropy formula, including why Rényi-2 and von Neumann entropies agree.
  2. Compute one star's four-edge entropy and a 2×22\times22×2 star block's twelve-edge entropy. Check the crossed-star rule.
  3. Form the Kitaev–Preskill wedge and Levin–Wen annular combinations on an L=12L=12L=12 torus and check −ln⁡2-\ln2−ln2 and −2ln⁡2-2\ln2−2ln2. Place each edge at its midpoint, h(x,y)h(x,y)h(x,y) at (x+12,y)(x+\tfrac12,y)(x+21​,y) and v(x,y)v(x,y)v(x,y) at (x,y+12)(x,y+\tfrac12)(x,y+21​), in the zero-based coordinates of §3.3. The Kitaev–Preskill regions are the three wedges of the disk of radius 4.84.84.8 about (6.01,6.013)(6.01,6.013)(6.01,6.013), offset slightly so that no midpoint lies on a cut, split by polar angle into thirds. The Levin–Wen regions are the annulus 1.6<r<4.81.6<r<4.81.6<r<4.8 with neither gap, the upper gap, the lower gap, or both gaps removed, a gap being the vertical strip of half-width 0.90.90.9 through the center on that side.

Interpret the measured normalized values −0.89±0.07-0.89\pm0.07−0.89±0.07, −0.90±0.09-0.90\pm0.09−0.90±0.09, −0.95±0.06-0.95\pm0.06−0.95±0.06 for 2×22\times22×2, 2×32\times32×3, 3×33\times33×3 arrays (PDF p. 3). Convert the last to nats. Why can small regions work at this fixed point, and why can noise move the result toward zero?

Hint

Only stabilizers that are identity on the traced-out sites survive. Their sum is a projector with flat nonzero spectrum. Every nonempty proper region of a GHZ state has one bit of entropy, even when disconnected.

Check against the rubric
  • Derives the reduced-state projector and its rank, rather than quoting an entropy law.
  • Computes supported ranks one and five, giving three and seven bits.
  • Gives the correct KP and LW signs and distinguishes the GHZ values.
  • Converts normalized units and interprets the measured spread correctly.
  • Distinguishes the fixed-point calculation from a claim of universality for arbitrary small noisy regions.
Show model solution

Choose a pure stabilizer ground state, fixing both logical Z values. Its projector is 2−n∑g∈Sg2^{-n}\sum_{g\in S}g2−n∑g∈S​g. Tracing out the complement removes every Pauli acting nontrivially there, leaving ρA=2−∣A∣∑g∈SAg\rho_A=2^{-|A|}\sum_{g\in S_A}gρA​=2−∣A∣∑g∈SA​​g. With rAr_ArA​ independent supported generators, the projector has rank 2∣A∣−rA2^{|A|-r_A}2∣A∣−rA​. One star's edges support that star: 4−1=34-1=34−1=3 bits. The 2×22\times22×2 block supports four stars and one enclosed plaquette: 12−5=712-5=712−5=7 bits. Four and eight crossed stars reproduce (b−1)ln⁡2(b-1)\ln2(b−1)ln2.

Exact local constraints and flat reduced spectra let small, well-chosen regions work at the fixed point. A completely mixed product state instead has S(A)=∣A∣ln⁡2S(A)=|A|\ln2S(A)=∣A∣ln2, with zero boundary-canceling subtractions. Loss of the relevant correlations can move the result toward zero; arbitrary noise need not do so monotonically. Break the boundary rule's hidden assumption

Replace the mixed patch by an ordinary disk with an all-smooth perimeter. Use a d×dd\times dd×d vertex grid with all its complete faces. Prove k=0k=0k=0 by rank counting and by homology. Then let the disk perimeter alternate between rough and smooth in 2s2s2s nonempty connected segments. Derive the encoded count and describe the minimum boundary-type change that permits k=1k=1k=1, keeping the topology a disk and adding no holes.

See Bravyi–Kitaev, PDF p. 5, Browne, PDF p. 104, and Dennis et al., PDF p. 7 Topological quantum memory, PDF p. 7 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1063/1.1499754. With an all-smooth exterior, hhh genuine smooth holes instead encode hhh qubits, paired by loops and boundary-to-hole strings.

Two alternating segments, one rough and one smooth, encode zero, as an all-one-type perimeter does. Four alternating segments encode one. To obtain them, convert two separated portions of the all-smooth perimeter to rough and rebuild their checks. A single converted portion is insufficient. The boundary separation and lattice width still set the distance.

You can now read a surface-code drawing as a check table and test whether recovery preserves an arbitrary stored state. Local checks reveal string endpoints; the residual winding or boundary-to-boundary path determines the logical action. Assume odd distance, independent single-type data errors, perfect checks and minimum-weight recovery. Then the first possible failure needs (d+1)/2(d+1)/2(d+1)/2 errors. At fixed distance and small ppp, that count is the leading power of the logical error.

Optional: follow the physics of LDPC codes to explore how changing locality and connectivity changes the matter picture.

Module 4 asks how to measure checks with faulty hardware without letting one ancilla fault spread into a damaging error. Module 5 asks how to choose a recovery from an imperfect history of those measurements.
